changes.old: The half coset introduces only constant phases and the already-correct algebraic parameter μ=λ²g; none of the character arguments divide by two modulo q. For the integer lift, the one possible zero-residue point is represented by 1 rather than 0. On a nonexceptional source fiber, fixing either free source to this point leaves at most one solution, while fixing the target to this point leaves at most two by strong Sidonicity. Thus its seam correction is O(1). On any fixed-target fiber, fixing one source to the seam point leaves at most two ordered pairs, hence the total seam correction is O(1). Exceptional source fibers were already handled exactly. The value X=1 is therefore included: source count zero and target limiting count p/2.
changes.new: The half coset introduces only constant phases and the already-correct algebraic parameter μ=λ²g; none of the character arguments divide by two modulo q. For the integer lift, the one possible zero-residue point is represented by 1 rather than 0. On a nonexceptional source fiber, fixing either free source to this point leaves at most one solution, while fixing the target to this point leaves at most two by strong Sidonicity. Thus its seam correction is O(1). On any fixed-target fiber, fixing one source to the seam point leaves at most two ordered pairs, hence the total seam correction is O(1). Exceptional source fibers were already handled exactly. The value X=1 is therefore included: the source count is zero; the target count is p/2+o(p) at a nonexceptional target and is at most two at the possible exceptional target. In all cases the uniform target upper bound remains valid.

changes.old: It suffices to allow O(1) exceptional vertices with O(p) total weighted incidence each, or more generally errors whose sum over all p seed vertices is o(p²). The constants may depend on the fixed W. In particular, no uniformity over a shrinking smoothing parameter is required.
changes.new: Part I proves this upper bound at every vertex, including the explicit exceptional fibers. More generally, O(1) exceptional vertices with O(p) total weighted incidence each would suffice, as would errors whose sum over all p seed vertices is o(p²). The constants may depend on the fixed W. In particular, no uniformity over a shrinking smoothing parameter is required.
